title: Adaptive KV Slewing and Hetero-Fallback Playbook
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: intermittent OOMs during sustained continuous-batching workloads where KV working sets spike transiently (LLM chat sessions with long context + background prefetch). Current eviction is largely reactive and coarse-grained which leads to retries, high tail latency, or full model fallbacks that degrade quality.

Goal: design and implement an orchestrated strategy that blends probabilistic kv-slewing (controlled background prefetch throttling that 'slews' working set growth), micro-hedged request admission, and a lane-based heterogeneous fallback playbook to avoid OOMs or fail gracefully with minimal user impact. The feature should provide deterministic SLO improvement on 95/99th latency p99 and reduce OOM-driven fallbacks by >70% on targeted workloads.

Scope: KV prefetch admission controller, slewing policy engine, micro-hedge (short hedged retries to mini-quantized or distilled model), fallback ladder definition and routing, canary rollout in Dedicated clusters, observability dashboards and alerting, unit+integration tests and performance baselines. Not in scope: full multi-tenant quota overhaul, long-term cross-instance global KV coordination (future).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Canary runs show >= 70% reduction in OOM incidents for target workload within 48h without increasing median latency by >5%. 2) Automated rollout that can be toggled per-customer and per-model variant. 3) Clear dashboard showing kv-slew state, admission drops, hedged-retry counts, and fallback triggers. 4) Unit/integration test coverage and runbook for incident postmortems.
success_metrics: OOM incidents (count) reduced by >=70% for selected clusters; p99 latency improves or stays within 5% of baseline; customer-visible fallback rate reduced; no elevation in error rates for other tenants.
risks: 1) Over-aggressive slewing could underutilize GPU leading to cost inefficiency. 2) Hedged retries may amplify load during systemic memory pressure. 3) Incorrect priority tagging could evict hot prefixes. 4) Edge cases with very long KV lifespans causing repeated micro-hedges.
design_notes:
We adopt a multi-signal approach: combine GPU resident occupancy, per-slot kv-hotness score, recent admission rate, and incoming sequence-length histogram to compute a slewing coefficient (0-1) per-serving-pool. Slew coefficient tunes prefetch window and admission headroom. When headroom is insufficient, the admission controller applies progressive degradation: token-dropping suggestions -> request-level micro-hedge (spawn a 50ms-limited hedged attempt against a distilled / lower-context model) -> route to readonly fallback with cached responses for idempotent prompts. Fallback ladder is parameterized per-model and per-customer.

Memory accounting: introduce ephemeral kv-tickets per-request that estimate worst-case delta. Tickets are probabalistic with conservative headroom margin and are reconciled on completion. KV eviction policy augmented with soft-reserve buckets for high-priority customers to avoid cascade evictions.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (week 1-2): instrumentation + signal fusion (occupancy, slot headroom, sequence histograms). Phase 2 (week 3): implement slewing coefficient and admission controller with toggle flags; local integration tests. Phase 3 (week 4): micro-hedge runtime paths and lightweight mini-model dock. Phase 4 (week 5): fallback ladder routing and dashboards + canary. Phase 5 (week 6): broader rollout, incident runbook update and postmortem playbook.
rollout_plan: Start with internal Dedicated clusters for lab runs; canary to 3 small customers (non-critical) for 72h; monitor OOMs, p99, hedged retry amplification. If stable, expand to larger customer cohorts, then to hosted with opt-in toggle. Provide kill-switch at route and tenant levels.
testing_plan: Synthetic workload harness that reproduces long-context spikes; soak tests for 48h; fault-injection tests to simulate sudden KV working set doubling; regression benchmark against runtime-1.19 baseline. Add unit tests for slewing math, deterministic ticketing, and fallback selection. Load tests run in CI with GPUs via perf-lab.
